title: Leg-1 broadcast is dead on arrival: deployer/owner is not an authorized withdrawer on any of the 3 old strategies, so the first mutating call (skimSurplus) reverts and no suite step grants the permission
location: script/SkimAndLeg1Migration.s.sol:196-200 (skim calls), :126-138 (preflight checks owner() only); root cause lib/vault/src/AYieldStrategy.sol:461-471 (skimSurplus onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer), :224-229 (modifier), :309 (setWithdrawer, the only grant path). Missing wiring belongs in DeployTempStableStakerAndMigrators.s.sol (step 1) or a leg-1 preflight.
description: `skimSurplus` is gated on the authorizedWithdrawers registry, which is fully separate from owner — the owner is never implicitly authorized. On live state the ONLY authorized withdrawer on YS_DOLA_OLD/YS_USDC_OLD/YS_USDE is the post-replace-sya SYA (0x3C69…8270, wired by ReplaceSYAMainnet step 12); authorizedWithdrawers[OWNER]==false on all three (verified on fork). SkimAndLeg1Migration calls skimSurplus as the owner EOA, and neither this script nor any other story-060 step calls setWithdrawer(OWNER, true). The script's preflight verifies owner() on all three strategies but never checks withdrawer status, so the failure is only discovered at execution. Empirically (fork preview, unmodified script, valid inputs): revert 'AYieldStrategy: unauthorized, only authorized withdrawers' at IOldYS(YS_DOLA_OLD).skimSurplus. In broadcast mode (--skip-simulation --slow) this would be a real failed mainnet tx and the suite halts at step 2 of 5.
impact: The story-060 migration suite cannot execute as written: step 2 deterministically fails before any migration occurs (fail-safe — no partial state, one wasted failed tx). Migration of the buggy DOLA/USDC strategies is blocked until out-of-band setWithdrawer transactions are crafted manually.

classification.assetImpact: None. The script reverts at its first mutating call (skimSurplus) before any funds move; fully atomic clean revert, no partial state.
attackPath: 1. Operator broadcasts leg1 as the owner EOA.
2. skimSurplus is onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer; authorizedWithdrawers[OWNER]==false on all three old strategies.
3. First call reverts 'unauthorized'; one wasted failed tx, no migration begun.
classification.likelihood: Deterministic on live state, but fails safe at the very first action with zero funds moved.
classification.assumptions: Owner has not separately granted itself withdrawer; fix is a one-line setWithdrawer(OWNER,true) in step 1 (and revoke in cleanup).
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond owner adding the missing authorization step.

evidence: side-effects.json executed[1] (exact revert), preconditionResults (missing check), fork reads: authorizedWithdrawers(OWNER)==false x3, authorizedWithdrawers(SYA)==true x3 on 0x90ce…7F9, 0x90af…470, 0xaC2e…f95. grep over all 5 suite scripts: zero setWithdrawer calls. Fork fixup (setWithdrawer(OWNER,true) x3 from the strategies' owner) lets preview and broadcast-equivalent complete end-to-end. side-effects.json clusterChecks[0].
recommendation: Add `setWithdrawer(OWNER_ADDRESS, true)` on the three old strategies to step 1 (inside the broadcast block, before the skims; the strategies' owner is the same signing EOA) and revoke in PostMigrationCleanup, OR route the skim through the SYA's own collection entry point. Add a preflight `require(authorizedWithdrawers(OWNER_ADDRESS))` so the script refuses to broadcast into a guaranteed failure.
dedupNotes: COLLAPSED two raw candidates with one root cause: deploy F2 (migrate:ys-swap-deploy/idx1) and leg1 idx0. Canonical entryPoint = migrate:ys-swap-leg1 (the script that actually reverts at its first mutation). The deploy-entry instance (F2) raised it as a forward-looking cluster flag; merged here. Per-entryPoint fingerprint namespacing means these would not auto-collide, but they share root cause MissingWithdrawerAuthorization and are presented as one finding.
sanitizationReason: New entry point migrate:ys-swap-leg1. Missing setWithdrawer authorization is a deterministic script-broadcast failure, not KI#10 admin-trust (no reckless/malicious owner; the script as written cannot succeed for ANY honest operator). Distinct from all 22 ledger entries (different entryPoint, root cause deployer-not-authorized-withdrawer). NEW.
severityJustification: Clean deterministic revert at the first mutation with no funds moved and a trivial one-line fix (setWithdrawer), so per the script-operational calibration this is a Low availability/operational footgun rather than Medium. It blocks the runbook but causes no partial state, no value leak, and no asset risk; the non-obvious missing-authorization wiring makes it a reportable footgun, not invalid admin-trust.
